vibe: Patch Tuesday is the centre of gravity, while powerful new agents make security capability and controllability the same story.

cyber.title: Microsoft September 2026 Patch Tuesday fixes 966 flaws, 2 zero-days
cyber.summary: Microsoft's September Patch Tuesday fixes a record-scale 966 flaws, including two zero-days. Windows and Microsoft estate owners should treat this as today's patching priority; SANS and the sysadmin megathread corroborate the release.

cyber.title: Adobe Patches Magento Zero-Day Exploited to Deploy Rust Backdoor and PHP Web Shell
cyber.summary: Adobe has patched an Adobe Commerce/Magento zero-day already used to deploy a Rust backdoor and PHP web shell. Internet-facing stores need the fix and a compromise hunt, not merely routine patch scheduling.

cyber.title: Hackers breach F5 BIG-IP APM devices to deploy Linux rootkit
cyber.summary: Attackers are compromising F5 BIG-IP APM appliances and installing a Linux rootkit. Check exposed appliances, vendor guidance and telemetry for persistence immediately.

cyber.title: SAP warns of maximum severity 'OVERPASS' kernel vulnerability
cyber.summary: SAP's OVERPASS kernel flaw carries the maximum severity rating. SAP teams should review the advisory and emergency-patch affected systems.

cyber.title: CISA warns of Chromium type-confusion zero-day actively exploited in attacks
cyber.summary: CISA says a Chromium type-confusion zero-day is being exploited. Update Chrome and Chromium-based browsers promptly and confirm managed fleets have actually received the fixed build.

cyber.title: ChatGPT Flaw Let a Planted Prompt Send a Victim's Gmail Data to Another Account
cyber.summary: A planted prompt could make ChatGPT send a victim's Gmail data to another account, a sharp example of indirect prompt injection crossing into connected services. Revisit connector permissions and least-privilege controls.

cyber.title: N-able issues patch for zero-day flaw
cyber.summary: N-able released another N-central zero-day fix, with reports describing a critical remote-code-execution issue. MSPs should prioritize patching because one console can expose many downstream customers.

cyber.title: A hacking tool built with AI can breach phones without a click
cyber.summary: Researchers demonstrated an AI-built tool capable of no-click phone compromise via WeChat, according to the Times. The important signal is automated exploit development becoming operational, not just theoretical.

cyber.title: Trezor customers hit with phishing calls and letters after shipping-partner breach
cyber.summary: Trezor customers are receiving convincing calls and physical letters after a shipping-partner breach. Treat any recovery-seed request as theft: never enter or disclose the seed outside the hardware wallet's trusted flow.

ai.title: OpenAI says GPT-6 Astra can find zero-days, but is also harder to monitor
ai.summary: OpenAI says GPT-6 Astra can discover zero-days, while stronger capabilities make its reasoning harder to monitor. That combination raises both defensive opportunity and governance risk for agentic security work.

ai.title: Muse: Meta's personal AI agent, features and capabilities
ai.summary: Meta launched Muse, a personal agent designed to shop, send email and plan trips, with privacy controls presented as a core feature. The real test will be whether users trust Meta with broad delegated authority.

ai.title: Mistral raises €3B
ai.summary: Mistral raised €3 billion to expand sovereign, open-weight AI infrastructure. It is a major bet that European buyers will pay for strategic independence as well as model quality.

ai.title: Google DeepMind Releases AlphaGenome Atlas
ai.summary: Google DeepMind released AlphaGenome Atlas, making genome-model predictions easier to explore. It is a substantial research resource, though practical clinical value will depend on validation and responsible use.

ai.title: On the Navier–Stokes Millennium Prize Problem
ai.summary: OpenAI claimed progress on the Navier–Stokes Millennium Prize problem, but mathematicians disputed attribution and process. Treat the scientific claim as consequential but contested until independent review settles it.

ai.title: ChatGPT Images 2.5
ai.summary: ChatGPT Images 2.5 adds a sketch-to-image workflow that turns rough drawings into detailed generations. It looks genuinely useful for fast visual ideation rather than merely another image-quality bump.

ai.title: How well do agents use test/verification techniques?
ai.summary: A careful look at how well coding agents actually use tests and verification finds meaningful gaps between producing code and proving it works. Useful reading for anyone designing agent workflows or review gates.

it.title: Google Cloud races to catch up in the AI deployment wars with Accenture deal
it.summary: Google Cloud's Accenture deal is aimed at accelerating enterprise AI deployment. For cloud engineers, the signal is that implementation capacity and governance are becoming as competitive as the models themselves.

it.title: Among European Companies That Use a CDN, Nearly 9 in 10 Use Cloudflare
it.summary: A survey argues nearly nine in ten European companies using a CDN rely on Cloudflare. Even allowing for methodology caveats, the concentration is a useful resilience and supplier-risk warning.

it.title: Jellyfin 12.0
it.summary: Jellyfin 12.0 landed with a large community response. It is the standout self-hosting release in today's feed and worth a look for home-media operators.

it.title: DaVinci Resolve 21.1
it.summary: DaVinci Resolve 21.1 is out. It is a meaningful update for video workflows, though less urgent than today's security and cloud stories.

videos.title: GPT-6 Astra Changes Everything
videos.verdict: WATCH — concise hands-on demonstrations plus a useful safety/monitorability discussion.
videos.summary: Two Minute Papers tests GPT-6 Astra on ray tracing and research-paper reproduction, then highlights a tension: safer observed behavior alongside reduced reasoning monitorability. High signal, enthusiastic presentation, and clearly separated demonstrations.

videos.title: Inside LockBit: How He Earned a Ransomware Gang’s Trust
videos.verdict: SKIM — potentially interesting LockBit access story, but no transcript was available, so confidence is limited.
videos.summary: An interview-style look inside LockBit and how trust was built with a ransomware gang. Metadata suggests original reporting, but the unavailable transcript prevents a reliable full digest.

videos.title: They Can Read Your Files
videos.verdict: SKIM — useful reminder; the first half carries the argument.
videos.summary: David Bombal explains that ordinary cloud-storage encryption does not stop the provider from accessing plaintext under controlled circumstances, and recommends client-side encryption for genuinely provider-blind storage. Sound basics, though framed dramatically.

videos.title: Claude Skills Explained: ELI5
videos.verdict: SKIM — a quick practical demo if you use Claude skills.
videos.summary: A short demonstration of an ELI5 skill that generates visual HTML explanations of complex topics. Useful workflow inspiration, but narrow and light on implementation detail.

videos.title: An Ancient Guide to Cybersecurity: 8 Lessons from The Art of War
videos.verdict: SKIM — solid fundamentals, but little is novel for experienced defenders.
videos.summary: IBM maps eight Art of War principles to attack-surface awareness, patching, deception, monitoring, segmentation, leadership and resource prioritisation. Clear security refresher rather than breaking insight.
